threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the underground' and get confused when your train's a day late.
Last week, saw a bloke on the 59 who kept insisting he was the reincarnation of Churchill. Pushed the driver to let him make a speech at the next stop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling flaming torches on Karl-Marx-Straße while waiting for a delayed bus. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find wild squirrels raiding beer gardens, somehow knowing exactly when to appear for the leftover pretzels.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell a long-time local by how they handle BART delays—calmly pull out a book instead of checking their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full formal attire juggling at the 16th St. BART, right next to a woman in sweats with a coffee. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the best food is in fancy restaurants; the real hidden gems are in the tiny takeaways tucked behind the main squares.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their enthusiasm for the Mercat de Gràcia, snapping photos of every stall while locals just grab their groceries.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Newbies always wait for the green man at Crossroads. The locals just bolt across, dodging bikes and cars like it's an Olympic sport.
Last night on the 59, a lad argued with the driver about his expired Oyster. Never seen someone so determined to ride for free!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a toddler selling homemade lemonade on the corner, while their mom bargained with a vintage dealer next door. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Prenzlauer Berg can you find a café that brews its coffee with water from the Spree. It’s like sipping a river's history.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they avoid the BART during a delay, opting for a bike instead. Tourists don't know the hidden gems in the alleys.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last night at Civic Center, a guy in a sequined suit did a dance off with a saxophonist while we waited for the 21. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every street festival means partying all night. In Gràcia, some locals just want to enjoy the quieter moments over coffee and a book.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still use an umbrella at the slightest hint of rain, oblivious to the locals' dance with the downpour.
